Register a block type

Source: R/block.R
sim_register_block_type.Rd

Every block in a model is an instance of a registered block type. A type declares its parameters and a build function that turns resolved parameter values into a block definition: ports, sizes, direct feedthrough, states, sample time and the functions that compute outputs, derivatives and discrete updates. The built-in library is registered when the package loads; sim_register_block_type() adds user types.

sim_register_block_type(
  type,
  build,
  params = list(),
  category = "user",
  description = "",
  portable = TRUE,
  overwrite = FALSE
)

Arguments

type

Type name (a single string).

build

Function of one argument, the named list of resolved parameters, returning a block definition.

params

Named list of parameter defaults. Use NULL for a required parameter.

category

Category used by sim_block_types().

description

One line description.

portable

TRUE when every parameter can be written to JSON, so the block can be saved with sim_write_json().

overwrite

Allow replacing an existing type.

Value

The type name, invisibly.

Details

The list returned by build(p) may contain:

  • inputs, outputs: integer vectors of port sizes. NA means the size is inherited from the connected signal (inputs) or computed by size_out (outputs). Names, when given, become port names.

  • size_out(in_sizes): returns output sizes once input sizes are known.

  • check_sizes(in_sizes, out_sizes): optional; signals an error when the resolved sizes are inconsistent.

  • feedthrough: logical, one per input port. TRUE when the outputs at time t depend on that input at time t.

  • nx, x0: number and initial value of continuous states.

  • nd, d0: number and initial value of discrete states.

  • sample: NULL for continuous (or inherited) blocks, otherwise c(period, offset). Discrete blocks compute outputs only at their sample hits and hold them in between.

  • output(t, x, d, u): returns a list with one numeric vector per output port (a plain vector is accepted for one port). u is a list of input vectors.

  • deriv(t, x, d, u): continuous state derivative.

  • update(t, x, d, u): next discrete state, called at sample hits after all outputs at that instant have been computed.

  • held0(d): initial held output of a discrete block before its first sample hit.

  • zc(t, x, d, u) and on_zc(i, direction, t, x, d, u): zero-crossing functions and their handler, which returns list(d = , x = , terminal = ). zc_direction gives one of "rising", "falling", "either" per component.

  • breakpoints(t0, tf): times where the block's output is discontinuous; the integrator restarts there.

All functions must be free of side effects: the solver calls them at trial points that it may later reject.

Examples

sim_register_block_type(
  "cube",
  build = function(p) list(
    inputs = NA, outputs = NA, feedthrough = TRUE,
    size_out = function(n) n,
    output = function(t, x, d, u) u[[1]]^3
  ),
  category = "math", description = "Elementwise cube"
)
m <- sim_model("cube_demo")
sim_add_block(m, "time", "t")
sim_add_block(m, "cube", "c")
sim_connect(m, "t", "c")
r <- sim_run(sim_compile(m), tspan = c(0, 2), times = c(0, 1, 2))
sim_signal(r, "c")
#> [1] 0 1 8
